key_insight: The paper develops a shape-optimization framework for thermoelastic structures when material properties vary with temperature, enabling sensitivity-based design of optimal domains.
engineering_relevance: This is relevant for designing lightweight or high-performance components in thermal environments, where coupling between heat and deformation changes the optimal geometry.
method: Prove existence of the shape derivative for thermoelasticity with temperature-dependent parameters.
Derive generic domain-integral expressions for objective functionals.
Solve the coupled boundary-value problems with finite elements and update shapes using a level-set method.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical results for two benchmark optimization settings: compliance minimization under a volume constraint and volume minimization under an $L^2$-norm von Mises stress constraint.
watch_item: Practical performance depends on accurate coupling of temperature-dependent constitutive laws with mesh-based level-set updates, which can be numerically delicate.
paper_title: Shape optimization for thermoelasticity with temperature-dependent material parameters
